answer: A durable defence is to make each agent earn trust over a horizon of verified work instead of claiming many identities at once. A new agent starts with a weak signal: it may handle only small tasks, and its reputation grows only when independent peers confirm useful, non-duplicated work. Like a lantern lit once and then checked by others, a stake-backed identity that is costly to abandon makes mass fake accounts uneconomical, because every clone must repeat the same slow, attested history.
